question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Apple)

calls.reasoning: Fiscal Q4 2026 (June 28-Sep 26) guided at +9-11% YoY on $102.47B, so $111.7-113.7B; consensus is about $113.4-113.6B. Over the last 4 quarters Apple hit the top of guidance (Q4 FY25: 8% vs 5-8%), beat it widely (Q1 FY26: 16% vs 10-12%), beat it (Q2: 17%) and landed upper-mid (Q3: 16% vs 14-17%). Supply constraints make revenue more predictable but cap the upside; Foxconn's record September, credited partly to Apple orders, is mildly positive. Median about $114.0B. No human prediction market was found (Polymarket and Manifold per the harness, Kalshi searched with no Apple revenue contract).
calls.dossier:
- Quarter: Apple fiscal Q4 2026 covers Jun 28-Sep 26, 2026. It includes launch week for iPhone 18 Pro, Watch S12/Ultra 4 and AirPods 5; iPhone Duo (Oct 23) is excluded (MacRumors, 2026-10-06).
- Report date: Nov 2, 2026, 1:30pm PT, which is after the question's scheduled resolution time of Oct 29 (MacRumors/9to5Mac, 2026-10-06).
- Guidance (Q3 call, 2026-07-30): total revenue +9 to 11% YoY, i.e. $111.7-113.7B on Q4 FY25 = $102.47B; FX headwind about 2.5pp; 'significantly greater' supply constraints on iPhone, Mac and iPad; iPhone growth guided to mid-teens.
- Consensus: about $113.37B (MarketBeat, Oct 2026) to $113.62B (AppleInsider/Yahoo). Analysts had modeled about 12% before the guide.
- Guide vs actual history: Q4 FY25 guided 5-8%, actual 8%. Q1 FY26 guided 10-12%, actual 16% ($143.8B). Q2 FY26 actual $111.2B (+17%), above the high end. Q3 FY26 guided 14-17%, actual 16% ($109.4B; consensus was $108.86B) (CNBC, Apple newsroom, Investing.com).
- Foxconn September 2026 revenue was a record NT$1.1T (+38.4% YoY); Q3 NT$3T (+46.8% YoY), credited to Apple new-model orders plus Nvidia GB300 racks (UDN, 2026-10-13). The AI mix muddies the Apple signal.
- Pegatron Q3 +50.8% YoY was driven by CSP/AI orders; analysts cite weak phone-season demand (UDN, 2026-10-13).
- Growth-to-dollar mapping on the $102.47B base: 9% = $111.7B, 10% = $112.7B, 11% = $113.7B, 12% = $114.8B, 13% = $115.8B, 15% = $117.8B.
- Status quo: Apple lands inside or above its guided range; a miss below the low end has not happened in the last 4 quarters.
- Resolution instrument: total net sales in Apple's Q4 FY26 8-K press release.
- Event window: the first revenue report after Sept 2026, expected Nov 2, 2026. As of Oct 13 the quarter is closed and the number is fixed but not yet reported.
- Searched without finding: any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold contract; late-October analyst revisions.

calls.reasoning: Apple guided FQ4 2026 revenue to +9-11% YoY on $102.47B ($111.7-113.7B); consensus is about $113.4-113.6B. Relative to the guidance midpoint, the last four quarters came in at -1.1, +5, +2.1 and +0.9pp, which applied here centers on about 11% growth, or roughly $113.8B. Sharply worse supply constraints and a 2.5pp FX headwind cap the upside, though the last two supply-limited quarters still beat the midpoint. Foxconn's record September is mildly supportive. I keep about 7% below $112B to cover a repeat of the FQ4 2025 low-end miss. No human market was found.
calls.reconciliation: The one factual dispute was the FQ4 2025 guide: Run 1 said 5-8% with the top hit; Runs 2-3 said 8-10% with a slight miss at 7.9%. This could not be checked on this run (no web access). Recollection matches Runs 2-3, so I treat FQ4 2025 as a borderline miss and keep real low-tail mass. Everything else matched across the dossiers: guide $111.7-113.7B, consensus about $113.4-113.6B, report date Nov 2, the beat history, and Foxconn. The remaining disagreement is judgment: how much the supply cap offsets the beat pattern. I center slightly above the top of the guide ($113.8B), because the recent constrained quarters still beat the midpoint by 1-2pp, and set the low tail between Run 1 and Runs 2-3 based on the one-in-four miss rate, not by averaging. I adopted the runs' reference class (Apple results vs its own guidance).
